SUBJECT:       CHRISTOPHER M. CRANE CLEAN ENERGY CENTER – REQUEST FOR
               INFORMATION FOR PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION AND RESOLUTION
               INSPECTION; INSPECTION REPORT 05000289/2027010

Dear Christopher Mudrick:

The purpose of this letter is to notify you that the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
staff will conduct a problem identification and resolution inspection at Christopher M. Crane
Clean Energy Center. Eric Miller, a Senior Resident Inspector from the NRC’s Region I office,
will lead the inspection team. The inspection will be conducted in accordance with Inspection
Manual Chapter 2562, “Light-Water Reactor Inspection Program for Restart of Reactor Facilities
following permanent Cessation of Power Operations,” dated April 24, 2025, utilizing
Inspection Procedure 71152, “Problem Identification and Resolution,” dated September 1, 2026
(Agencywide Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS) Accession
No. ML26231A398) and Operating Experience Smart Sample 2020/01, “Flex Equipment Design
Control, Maintenance, and Testing,” dated October 21, 2020.

The inspection will assess the effectiveness of your problem identification and resolution
program in identifying, prioritizing, evaluating, and correcting problems as well as incorporation
of recent operating experience. This inspection will also assess your program for raising
concerns under the established safety conscious work environment. In addition, the inspection
will assess the site’s performance to reimplement the mitigation strategies for flexible coping
strategies. The onsite inspection is scheduled for the weeks of January 11 and January 25,
2027.

In order to minimize the inspection impact on the site and to ensure a productive inspection for
both parties, we have enclosed a request for information needed for the inspection. It is
important that all of these documents are up-to-date and complete in order to minimize the
number of additional documents requested during the preparation and/or the onsite portions of
the inspection. Insofar as possible, this information should be provided electronically to the lead
inspector by December 14, 2026.
 C. Mudrick                                      2


If there are any questions about the inspection or the material requested in the enclosure,
please contact the lead inspector at 610-337-6901 or via e-mail at eric.miller@nrc.gov.

This letter does not contain new or amended information collection requirements subject to the
Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.). Existing information collection
requirements were approved by the Office of Management and Budget, Control Number 3150-
0011. The NRC may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a
request for information or an information collection requirement unless the requesting document
displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget Control Number.

This letter and its enclosure will be made available for public inspection and copying at
http://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/adams.html and at the NRC Public Document Room in
accordance with Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations 2.390, “Public Inspections,
Exemptions, Requests for Withholding.”

                          REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR
           BIENNIAL PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION AND RESOLUTION INSPECTION

Inspection Report:                    05000289/2027010

Onsite Inspection Dates:              January 11 through January 15, 2027
                                      January 25 through January 29, 2027

Inspection Guidance:                  IP 71152, Problem Identification and Resolution, dated
                                      September 1, 2026

                                      Operating Experience Smart Sample 2020/01. Flex
                                      Equipment Design Control, Maintenance, and Testing,
                                      dated October 21, 2020

Lead Inspector:                       Eric Miller, Senior Resident Inspector
                                      610-337-5024
                                      eric.miller@nrc.gov


The following information is requested by December 14, 2026, or sooner, to facilitate inspection
preparation. The requested information is for the period from September 1, 2024 through
October 5, 2026 (Present), with specific requests, as noted, that cover information for the two
years prior to cessation of operations.

An information gathering trip is currently scheduled for December 3, 2026. The purpose of this
trip is for the team lead to familiarize themselves with the site organization including meeting
with the Employee Concerns Program Manager, receive an overview of the corrective action
program, and to finalize remaining administrative arrangements for the inspection.

Feel free to contact the lead inspector as soon as possible if you have any questions regarding
this information request. Please provide the information electronically in ‘pdf’ files, Excel, or
other searchable formats, preferably on an internet database system (e.g., OneDrive). The files
should contain descriptive names, be indexed, and hyperlinked to facilitate ease of use.
Information in “lists” should contain enough information to be easily understood by someone
who is not familiar with the site.


I.   General

     1. Organization charts, phone list, and list of system engineers.

     2. List of system numbers/designations and a list of system engineers assigned to those
        systems.

     3. Copy of the Quality Assurance Manual and Quality Assurance Topical Report.

     4. A schedule of the date/time/location of meetings associated with implementation of the
        correction action program such as Plan-of-the-Day, Station Ownership Committee
        (SOC), Management Review Committee (MRC), etc.

     5. Probability risk assessment (PRA) risk-ranking of systems, including a chart with highest
        risk systems/components.


                                                                                       Enclosure
                        REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR

II. Corrective Actions

   1. Copy of procedures related to the corrective action program, including issue
      identification, cause evaluations, corrective actions, trending, self-assessments,
      operability determinations, work management, operating experience, etc.

   2. List of all corrective action program deficiency reports (IRs, ARs, etc.) initiated after
      September 1, 2024 – in electronic spreadsheet format – include the following (as
      applicable): system number/designation, date initiated, significance level, status (open or
      closed), title/short description, department, date closed or due, and if possible, the
      number of due date extensions.

   3. List of Level 1, 2, and 3 corrective action program document evaluations (IRs, ARs, etc.)
      initiated between January 1, 2017 and cessation of operations – in electronic
      spreadsheet format – include the following (as applicable): system number/designation,
      date initiated, significance level, status (open or closed), title/short description,
      department, date closed or due, and if possible, the number of due date extensions.

   4. List of all root cause evaluations (RCE), apparent cause evaluations (ACE), common
      cause evaluations (CCE), and work group evaluations (WGE), performed after
      September 1, 2024 – include number, title, eval type, and date completed.

   5. Matrix of the total number of condition/issue reports generated annually and monthly
      since September 1, 2024.

   6. List of open temporary modifications, adverse condition monitoring plans, operator work
      arounds, and operability evaluations at the cessation of operations – include tracking
      no., system id., title/short description, date initiated, and date corrective action(s)
      due/work order(s) scheduled dating back to cessation of operations.

   7. List of hot functional testing that will be performed a week before testing occurs. Provide
      test number, test name/title, latest revision, and associated work order.

   8. List of restart critical preventive maintenance tasks organized by system and level of
      component criticality and associated due dates.

   9. List of FLEX equipment conditions or deficiencies documented in the corrective action
      program since May 1, 2017.


III. Operating Experience

   1. List of operating experience reviews, including Part 21s and NRC generic
      communications (i.e., Information Notices, Generic Letters, Bulletins) initiated since
      September 1, 2024. Provide tracking number, title/short description, date initiated, date
      due or closer, significance level, evaluation class/type, status, department, and, if
      possible, the number of due date extensions.




                                               2
                        REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR
         BIENNIAL PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION AND RESOLUTION INSPECTION


   2. List of industry operating experience issues (NSSS vendor reports, EPRI Reports, and
      OPEX reports from other facilities) entered into the corrective action program for review
      since September 1, 2024. Provide tracking number, title/short description, date initiated,
      date due or closed, significance level, evaluation class/type, status, department, and, if
      possible, the number of due date extensions.

   3. Provide list of correction action program tracking items generated as a result of issues
      identified during the operating experience reviews and assessment. Provide tracking
      number, title/short description, date initiated, date due or closer, significance level,
      evaluation class/type, status, department, and, if possible, the number of due date
      extensions.

   4. Copy of Flex Strategy implementation documents, including RSG documentation.


IV. Safety Conscious Work Environment and ECP

   1. Access to a list of all ECP cases and contacts initiated since September 1, 2024.
      Include a list of IRs generated as a result of these reviews. (Will be reviewed onsite to
      maintain confidentiality)

   2. A copy of all safety culture reviews (audits, assessments, surveys, trend review, etc.)
      initiated since September 1, 2024. Include a list of any IRs generated as a result of
      these reviews. (Will be reviewed onsite to maintain confidentiality)
